turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... I've been working on this memorial for my brother, and it’s just gotten a lot bigger than I meant it to. 

I’ve been spending most of my days lately just chasing down the right songs, calling folks up, planning out displays and trips. It feels important to get it right, but my wife is pretty concerned. She says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I normally do. So... she really wanted me to come talk to you about it.

symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes an excessive increase in goal-directed activity, spending all their time planning an elaborate memorial to the point of neglecting regular routines and responsibilities.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Over these past weeks while you've been so focused on the memorial, have you noticed you're needing much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm sleeping about the same amount I always do. I might wake up a bit early sometimes thinking about the displays or who I need to call next, but I wouldn't say I need less sleep. And I don't exactly feel full of energy... just, well, very focused on getting this done for him.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly denies needing less sleep or feeling rested with less sleep, stating they sleep about the same amount as usual.

turns.doctor_question: How long ago did your brother pass away, and when did you start feeling this intense pull to work on the memorial?
turns.patient_response: He passed away about two months ago. And... well, that's pretty much when all this started. I began working on his tribute right after we lost him, so this whole thing has been going on for about two months now.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about the memorial throughout the day, do those thoughts feel unwanted or intrusive—like they force their way in and cause you distress—or do they feel more like a comforting way you want to spend your time thinking about your brother?
turns.patient_response:
No, they don't feel unwanted at all. It's not like they force their way into my head and upset me or anything like that. 

I actually want to be thinking about it. It's... well, it's a way to feel close to him, I guess. I just want to make sure I do right by him, so spending my time on it feels like the right thing to do. It definitely doesn't cause me any distress to think about the memorial, it's just important to me.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies that the thoughts about the memorial are intrusive, unwanted, or distressing, stating they are welcome and meaningful.

turns.doctor_question: Has this focus on the memorial caused ongoing tension or problems in your marriage or other relationships, or affected your ability to keep up with important responsibilities?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yes, it has caused some problems. I suppose I've dropped a lot of my usual activities. I haven't been to my walking group or my book club in a while, and the garden is just completely overgrown at this point. 

And... well, I've upset some folks at the senior center. They say everything I talk about now is just the memorial display, and they get tired of it. As for my wife, she's definitely feeling the strain. She tells me that our whole day just revolves around trying to calm me down, or her trying to talk me out of making another phone call, or taking another trip for supplies, or getting into another argument with someone about it. So, yes, it's definitely affecting things.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from how this has affected your relationships and activities, have you personally been feeling very sad, guilty, or hopeless since your brother passed away?
turns.patient_response:
No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... of course I miss him, but I haven't really been feeling sad or hopeless or anything like that. And I don't feel guilty, either. 

I guess most folks expect you to be sitting around crying when you lose a brother, but I haven't felt down. Mostly I just feel... well, driven to get this memorial finished. So no, I haven't had those kinds of feelings.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling sad, crying, or feeling down.
symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient explicitly states they do not feel guilty.
symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient explicitly denies feeling hopeless.

turns.doctor_question: When your wife or others try to get you to slow down or stop working on the memorial, do you find yourself feeling unusually irritable, angry, or on edge with them?
turns.patient_response: Well, yeah, I do. I mean, I'll feel really... lit up, you know? Full of purpose one minute, thinking about how the whole town is finally going to understand our family when they see this. But then... yeah, if my wife or someone at the senior center tries to slow me down or questions what I'm doing with the display, I just snap at them. I get really irritable. It's like they're just getting in the way of what needs to be done.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing an elevated, purposeful mood ('lit up') shifting quickly to irritability and snapping at others when interrupted or questioned.

turns.doctor_question: Besides feeling driven to finish the memorial, have you noticed feeling unusually confident, special, or like you have grand plans or abilities that go beyond how you'd normally see yourself?
turns.patient_response: Well, I don't know about grand plans or feeling special, exactly. I mean, I just know this memorial is important and I'm the one who has to do it right. But I don't think I have any special powers or anything like that. I'm just focused on getting this done.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient denies having grand plans, feeling special, or having special powers, directly rejecting inflated self-esteem or grandiosity.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed your thoughts racing or jumping quickly from one idea to another—more than you're used to—especially when you're working on the memorial?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I definitely have. It's like... my mind just won't stop. It keeps jumping from one idea to the next. One minute I'm thinking about how to build a display case, and then suddenly I'm planning a road trip to find this cousin I haven't seen in years. And then, before I know it, I'm trying to remember a verse from some old ballad my brother liked. It all just comes so fast, and I can't even slow it down enough to write it all out in order. It's just... constant.

symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient confirms racing thoughts and flight of ideas, describing their mind rapidly jumping from one concept to another and being unable to slow it down.

turns.doctor_question: Over the past two months, has this heightened, irritable, 'lit up' feeling and drive to work on the memorial been present nearly every day for at least a full week at a time, without letting up?
turns.patient_response: I... I'm not really sure about that. I haven't exactly been keeping track of the days on a calendar or anything. I mean, it's been happening a lot lately, this whole drive to get it done, but I couldn't tell you if it's been every single day for a full week straight without a break. I just know I've been focused on it pretty heavy for a while now.

turns.doctor_question: Before your brother passed away, had you ever gone through a period—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually high-energy, irritable, or 'lit up' like this, or a period of significant depression, at any other time in your life?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little down, or times where I had some energy, just like anybody else. But nothing like this. Nothing that lasted for weeks or where I felt this... this driven, or this irritable. Before he passed, things were just pretty normal, really. I never had anything like what's happening right now.
